Shehu Sani, who represented Kaduna Central in the 8th Senate, criticised those threatening violence and war over the forthcoming elections, saying they have a naive, detached understanding of armed conflict.
Mr Sani, in a statement on Facebook, argued that those beating the drums of war have never encountered real security threats, such as the banditry and terrorism in northern Nigeria.
He said many of them would not dare travel along the region’s volatile highways at night.
“Most people who are threatening war or violence because of elections have never in their lives come face to face with bandits or the Ansaru people,” Mr Sani stated.
“I’m very sure they don’t even dare to travel from Abuja to Kaduna, or Funtua to Gusau or Sokoto, or Maiduguri to Potiskum by 12 midnight,” he added.
The former senator observed that many online agitators trivialise the devastating reality of war, equating it to harmless digital disputes or entertainment.
“They think of war as social media altercations in the comment sections or simply video games,” he said.

Mr Sani urged younger Nigerians who may be unaware of the country’s past ethno-religious crises to research the violent clashes that rocked Kaduna State over two decades ago.
“For those who are too young to know, just Google what happened in Kaduna in 2000 to 2002. It will give you a little idea of what war means,” he added, warning against rhetoric capable of plunging the nation into avoidable turmoil.
Mr Sani’s message is against the rising election fever in Nigeria, which will hold its eighth regular general election since 1999 next year.
